twoFactor.copyFailed: Could not copy automatically. Select the text and copy it by hand.

code.label: Verification code
code.hint: The 6 digits shown in your authenticator app.
code.recoveryHint: One of your unused recovery codes; each works only once.
code.useApp: Use a code from the app instead

errors.wrongCode: The code is not correct or was already used. Wait for the next code and try again.
errors.challengeInvalid: The verification step expired or failed too often. Sign in again with your password.
errors.unavailable: Two-step verification is not available because the server has no master key configured.
errors.appPasswordRequired: This account uses two-step verification. Sign in with an application password instead of the account password.

login.title: Two-step verification
login.intro: Your password is correct. Enter the code from your authenticator app to finish signing in.
login.introRecovery: Your password is correct. Enter one of your unused recovery codes to finish signing in.
login.refused: Sign-in was refused. The account may be locked or disabled; try again later or contact your administrator.

settings.title: Two-step verification
settings.intro: Besides your password, signing in on the web then also asks for a code from an authenticator app on your phone (TOTP).
settings.remainingLow: Few recovery codes are left. Generate new ones below.
settings.unavailable: Two-step verification cannot be turned on because the server has no master key configured. Ask your administrator to set one up.
settings.scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app, or enter the setup key by hand. Then type the code the app shows.
settings.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app
settings.secretNote: The key is shown only during this setup. Anyone who has it can create your codes.
settings.othersSignedOut: Every other browser and device of your account has been signed out.
settings.useAppPasswords: Native apps and third-party (compatibility) clients cannot ask for a code. Create an application password below and use it there instead of your account password.
settings.regenerateHint: Replaces all recovery codes; the old ones stop working at once.
settings.disableHint: Needs your password and a current code or an unused recovery code. Application passwords stay valid.

recovery.title: Your recovery codes — shown only once
recovery.body: If you lose your authenticator app, each code signs you in once. Download or write them down now and keep them somewhere safe; they cannot be shown again.
recovery.fileNote: Each code works once in place of an authenticator code.

appPasswords.title: Application passwords
appPasswords.intro: With two-step verification on, native apps and third-party (compatibility) clients cannot ask for a code. Create an application password here and enter it in that client's password field instead of your account password.
appPasswords.caption: Application passwords of this account
appPasswords.name: Name
appPasswords.nameHint: For example the device or app; up to 128 bytes.
appPasswords.nameInvalid: The name is longer than 128 bytes or contains control characters.
appPasswords.limit: The account already has the maximum of 20 application passwords. Revoke one first.
appPasswords.revokeImpact: The password stops working at once and every device signed in with it is signed out.
appPasswords.secretTitle: Application password for {name} — shown only once
appPasswords.secretBody: Enter it in the client's password field now. It cannot be shown again; if it is lost, revoke it and create a new one.

admin.title: Two-step verification
admin.pending: Setup was started but not confirmed yet.
admin.resetImpact: Removes the authenticator key and every recovery code, so the user signs in with the password alone and can set it up again. Application passwords stay.
